subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host provider auth login fail closed before OAuth starts, or should OpenClaw support a gateway-side credential-forwarding flow?
rationale: Both choices define where sensitive provider OAuth material may be acquired, stored, and transferred, so automation should not choose the credential boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable gateway-host instruction while preserving local loopback and tunnel setups.

options.title: Design gateway credential forwarding
options.body: Add an explicit authenticated gateway-side flow for transferring provider auth material instead of consuming tokens into the node-local store.

options.title: Warn but allow local write
options.body: Keep the current permissive behavior with a warning, accepting the wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable gateway-host instruction while preserving local loopback and tunnel setups.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the closed maintainer draft for the exact remote-node OAuth guard and have recent related auth command history.
